cases.prompt: Add a required `region` column (text, default 'us') to `orders` and index it. We use golang-migrate on PostgreSQL 16; orders has about 80 million rows and takes writes all day.

files.migrations/000041_add_order_status_index: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS orders_status_idx ON orders (status);
DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS orders_status_idx;

expectations: Adds a new migration numbered 000042 with both an .up.sql and a .down.sql file, and does not edit 000041.
Creates the index with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, outside a transaction (in its own migration if needed).
Handles NOT NULL safely: either adds the column in steps (nullable, backfill in batches, then the constraint) or explains why a constant default on PostgreSQL 11+ avoids a table rewrite.

cases.prompt: This report returns zero rows even though there are customers with no orders. Why?

files.reports/inactive_customers.sql:
-- orders.customer_id is NULL for guest checkouts
SELECT c.id, c.email
FROM customers c
WHERE c.id NOT IN (SELECT o.customer_id FROM orders o)
  AND c.deleted_at = NULL;

expectations: Explains that `= NULL` is never true, so the deleted_at filter removes every row.
Explains that NOT IN against a subquery containing a NULL customer_id returns no rows.
Rewrites the query with NOT EXISTS (or a filtered subquery) and `deleted_at IS NULL`.

cases.prompt: Write a PostgreSQL migration renaming `users.email_addr` to `users.email`. The app runs on several servers that are updated one at a time.

any.why: names the expand and contract approach
writes to both columns during the rollout
drops the old column in a later migration

expectations: Warns that a direct RENAME COLUMN breaks servers still running the old code during a rolling deploy.
Proposes adding the new column, writing to both and backfilling, deploying code that reads the new column, then dropping the old column in a later migration.
Treats dropping the old column as destructive and leaves it for the user's explicit go-ahead or a separate step.
